Upholden
up-hol'dn
pp. (held up; sustained; supported — the older participle of uphold)
From up and hold, with the strong participial ending the Authorized Version preserves; modern English says upheld. The picture is a hand placed underneath something that would otherwise go down.

Biblical Definition

Two occurrences, and they answer a question worth asking: what holds a man up, and what holds a throne up? Of a man, and the agency is words: “Thy words have upholden him that was falling, and thou hast strengthened the feeble knees” (Job 4:4). This is Eliphaz reminding Job of his own former ministry, and the irony is thick — the counsel Job once gave others is about to fail him from the mouths of his friends. But the observation itself is true and the Bible endorses it elsewhere: speech holds people up. A man falling has been caught by a sentence more than once. Of a throne: “Mercy and truth preserve the king: and his throne is upholden by mercy” (Pro 20:28). Not by force, not by revenue, not by fear — by mercy and truth together, which is the pairing Scripture uses of God's own character. Behind both stands the hand that does the actual holding: “I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness” (Isa 41:10); and “Though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down: for the LORD upholdeth him with his hand” (Psa 37:24).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines uphold as to lift on high; to elevate; to support; to sustain; to keep from falling or declining; and to keep from being lost.

expand to see more

UPHO'LD, v.t. [up and hold.] pret. and pp. upheld. Upholden is obsolete.

1. To lift on high; to elevate.

2. To support; to sustain; to keep erect; to keep from falling.

Thy words have upholden him that was falling. Job 4.

3. To keep from declining; to support in any state. His throne is upholden by mercy. Prov. 20. 4. To continue without failing.

Key Scripture

Job 4:4 — "Thy words have upholden him that was falling, and thou hast strengthened the feeble knees."

Proverbs 20:28 — "Mercy and truth preserve the king: and his throne is upholden by mercy."

Isaiah 41:10 — "Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness."

Psalm 37:24 — "Though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down: for the LORD upholdeth him with his hand."

Modern Corruption

Power is assumed to be upheld by strength, and speech is assumed to be weightless — and Scripture reverses both.

expand to see more

Proverbs 20:28 is a startling piece of political theology: a throne is upheld by mercy. Every instinct of statecraft says otherwise — a ruler is secured by power, wealth, surveillance, or the fear he can generate. Solomon, who had all four, says the thing that actually holds a throne up is mercy and truth, the same pair used of the LORD Himself in Exodus 34:6. That is not a sentimental claim. A ruler who is neither merciful nor truthful must hold his place by force alone, and force is expensive and eventually insufficient. The Christian magistrate is a minister of God for good, and the qualities that keep him in place are the qualities of the God he serves.

Job 4:4 cuts the other way against a culture that treats words as weightless while also treating them as weapons. Eliphaz's observation is accurate: Job's words had held up men who were falling and strengthened feeble knees. What follows in the book is the demonstration that words can also crush, because Eliphaz and his friends proceed to spend thirty chapters doing exactly that to a man already on the ground. The same instrument that catches a falling man can finish him. That is why James puts the tongue at the centre of practical religion, and why the church's ordinary ministry of encouragement is not a minor thing — it is a hand under an elbow, and the hand under all of it is God's own (Isa 41:10).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew qum (H6965), to raise up, establish; sa'ad (H5582), to support, sustain; tamak (H8551), to grasp, uphold.

expand to see more

Hebrew yeqimun (H6965) — they raised up, set on his feet; Job 4:4, of words holding a falling man.

Hebrew sa'ad (H5582) — to support, uphold, sustain; Proverbs 20:28, of the throne held by mercy.

Hebrew chesed we'emeth (H2617, H571) — mercy and truth; the pair of Exodus 34:6, here holding up a king.

Hebrew tamakti (H8551) — I have grasped, upheld; Isaiah 41:10, the right hand of His righteousness.

Hebrew somekh (H5564) — upholding, leaning upon; Psalm 37:24, the LORD's hand under the falling man.

Usage

"“Thy words have upholden him that was falling” — and the same friends then crushed him."

"“His throne is upholden by mercy” — not by force, which runs out."

"“Though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down” — the hand is underneath."
